name: Recorded music & licensing
one_line: Owns and licenses recorded songs. Three major labels control the biggest catalogs that streaming royalties flow back to.
sells: Recorded songs and the rights to use them: streams, physical records, and licenses for sync (film/TV/ads), performance and artist services
customers: Music and video streaming services (Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube), social and short-video platforms, radio, film/TV/advertising, and fans
suppliers: Recording artists and songwriters, studios, music publishers, and distribution/aggregation services

revenue.note: MIDiA Research: $36.2B in 2024 (+6.5% YoY), or $32.1B excluding expanded rights; streaming was $22.2B (61.3% of the total). The narrower IFPI wholesale measure put 2025 revenue at $31.7B (+6.4%), with paid streaming 52.4% and 837M paid subscribers. Shares below are % of the MIDiA $36.2B total.

structure.why: Three major labels - Universal, Sony and Warner - take roughly two-thirds of global recorded-music revenue (~65%); the rest is a fragmented tail of independent labels (~29.7%) and self-releasing artists (~5.5%). Control of the biggest back catalogs is the durable moat.
structure.hhi_note: HHI from the three majors' shares only (UMG, Sony, WMG). The ~35% independent and artists-direct remainder is fragmented across many firms with no comparable published single-firm shares, so it adds little to HHI.

econ: Recorded music is a near-zero-marginal-cost good: once a track is made, each extra stream costs almost nothing, so value comes from owning the copyright and a deep back catalog. Three major labels hold about two-thirds of revenue, and their catalogs are the durable asset that streaming royalties flow back to.

companies.name: Universal Music Group (UMG)
companies.share_basis: share of global recorded-music revenue, 2024 (computed from MIDiA's stated UMG revenue of $10.5B over the $36.2B total)
companies.note: MIDiA reports UMG lost about 100 basis points of share in 2024.

companies.name: Sony Music Group
companies.share_basis: share of global recorded-music revenue, 2024 (MIDiA Research)
companies.note: MIDiA: Sony's recorded-music revenue rose 10.2% in 2024, share up ~700 basis points.

companies.name: Warner Music Group (WMG)
companies.share_basis: share of global recorded-music revenue, 2024 (derived as the residual of MIDiA's total after UMG 29.0%, Sony 21.7%, independent labels 29.7% and artists-direct 5.5%)
companies.note: Share derived as a residual; MIDiA did not state WMG's percentage in the cited post.

products_note: Flagship label families as of Nov 2026, from the majors' own sites (these are long-standing divisions, not volatile). Shares are MIDiA Research estimates of each firm's share of global recorded-music revenue for 2024; Sony's is stated, UMG's is computed from MIDiA's stated revenue, and Warner's is the residual. The map's 'All others' block (~35%) is the independent-label (~29.7%) and artists-direct (~5.5%) long tail, which has no single comparable firm share.
